source_text: Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδειμεν, Θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ Σωτήρ. Αἰσχυνθήσονται καὶ ἐντραπήσονται πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ. Ἀντίκεινται δὲ αὐτῷ οἱ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ τῆς αὐτῆς τῷ Πατρὶ οὐσίας, καὶ πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν, καὶ οἱ τὸ πάθος αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν ἐπαισχυνόμενοι. Οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται γνῶναι Θεὸν, ἐὰν μὴ τὸν σταυρωθέντα καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντα ὁμολογήσῃ σὺν τῷ ἀποστόλῳ Θωμᾷ Κύριον καὶ Θεὸν τὸν λέγοντα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις αὐτοῦ· Εἰ γὰρ ἐγνώκειτέ με, καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου ἐγνώκειτε ἂν, καὶ ἀπάρτι γινώσκετε αὐτὸν, καὶ ἑωράκατε αὐτόν. Λέγει αὐτῷ Φίλιππος· Κύριε, δεῖξον ἡμῖν τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ ἀρκεῖ ἡμῖν. Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τοσοῦτον χρόνον μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωκάς με; Φίλιππε, ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ ἑώρακε τὸν Πατέρα μου. Καὶ πῶς σὺ λέγεις· Δεῖξον ἡμῖν τὸν Πατέρα; Οὐ πιστεύεις, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστι; Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ, οὐκ ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ. Ὁ δὲ Πατήρ μου ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων, αὐτὸς ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα. Πιστεύετέ μοι, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρί μου, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστιν. Εἰ δὲ μὴ, διὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτὰ πιστεύετέ μοι. Ἔργον δὲ ἦν τοῦ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς τὸ ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια· ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια· Εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ, φησὶν, ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια· Περὶ οὗ ὁ Λουκᾶς φησιν· Εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν δακτύλῳ Θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω 1020 τὰ δαιμόνια. Ὅτε γὰρ ἡ Γραφὴ τὸν Χριστὸν βραχίονα ὀνομάζει τοῦ Πατρὸς, τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα δάκτυλον Θεοῦ καλεῖ· καὶ ὅτε δὲ τὸν Υἱὸν Θεοῦ Λόγον ὀνομάζει, τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα ἐμφύσημα τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγει. Καὶ πάλιν λέγει ὁ Ἀπόστολος· Ὅταν παραδιδῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν. Δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρις ἂν θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. Ἔσχατος ἐχθρὸς καταργεῖται ὁ θάνατος· πάντα γὰρ ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. Ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ, ὅτι Πάντα ὑποτέτακται, δῆλον, ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα. Ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ᾖ ὁ Θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι. Περὶ τῆς ὑποταγῆς τοῦ κόσμου λέγει τῆς ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποτεταγμένης. Περὶ γὰρ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ τῆς θεϊκῆς Δανιὴλ ἐξέφρασε λέγων· Καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος. Καθὼς καὶ ὁ Λουκᾶς λέγει τὸν ἄγγελον Γαβριὴλ εἰρηκέναι πρὸς τὴν Παρθένον περὶ τοῦ Κυρίου· Καὶ βασιλεύσει, φησὶν, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος. Ὁ δὲ Ἀπόστολος λέγει τέλος ἔχειν τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ. Δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν, φησὶν, ἄχρις ἂν θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ Δαβίδ· Εἶπε, φησὶν, ὁ Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
thought_title: The Son's subjection is the subjection of his flesh
orientation: Marcellus is arguing that the Son's subjection spoken of by Paul belongs to his incarnate flesh, not to his eternal divine kingdom, and he is citing Scripture to show that the Father works through the Son and the Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: You for are the God, and not we knew, God of Israel Savior. They will be ashamed and they will be turned in themselves all the ones opposing him. [They] oppose but him the [ones] not confessing him and the Spirit of him [to be] of the same with the Father substance, and besides him not to be God, and the [ones] the passion of him and the poverty being ashamed of. No one for is able to know God, if not the [one] crucified and from dead risen [one] he confesses with the apostle Thomas Lord and God the [one] saying to the apostles of him: If for you had known me, also the Father of me you would have known, and from now you know him, and you have seen him. Says to him Philip: Lord, show to us the Father, and it suffices to us. Says to him the Jesus: So much time with you I am, and not you have known me? Philip, the [one] having seen me has seen the Father of me. And how you say: Show to us the Father? Not you believe, that I in the Father, and the Father in me is? The words which I speak, not from myself I speak. The but Father of me in me remaining, he does the works. You believe me, that I in the Father of me, and the Father in me is. If but not, because of the works themselves you believe me. Work but was of God Father the to cast out the demons; in Spirit but holy he said to cast out the demons: If but I, he says, in Spirit of God I cast out the demons; About which the Luke says: If but I in finger of God I cast out 1020 the demons. When for the Scripture the Christ arm names of the Father, the holy Spirit finger of God calls; and when but the Son of God Word names, the holy Spirit breath of God says. And again says the Apostle: When he hands over the kingdom to the God and Father, when he abolishes all rule and all authority and power. It is necessary for him to reign until he puts all the enemies under the feet of him. Last enemy is abolished the death; all things for he subjected under the feet of him. When but he says, that All things have been subjected, clear, that except of the [one] having subjected to him the all things. When but are subjected to him the all things, then also himself the Son will be subjected to the [one] having subjected to him the all things, in order that may be the God the all things in all. About the subjection of the world he speaks of the in flesh of him having been subjected. About for the kingdom of him the divine Daniel expressed saying: And of the kingdom of him not will be end. Just as also the Luke says the angel Gabriel to have said to the Virgin about the Lord: And he will reign, he says, into the age and of the kingdom of him not will be end. The but Apostle says end to have the kingdom of him. It is necessary for him to reign, he says, until he puts all the enemies under the feet of him. Likewise but also the David: Said, he says, the Lord to the Lord of me: Sit at right of me, until I put the enemies of you footstool of the feet of you.

choices.english: of the same being as the Father
choices.why: The glossary requires 'being' for οὐσία in the context of consubstantiality, and the phrase is a direct statement of the Son and Spirit sharing the Father's being.
rejected: of the same substance as the Father

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'poverty' for πτωχεία, referring to the Son's voluntary lowliness in the incarnation.

choices.term: ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια
choices.english: and in the Holy Spirit he said to cast out demons
choices.why: The source has the infinitive ἐκβάλλειν with εἶπεν, meaning 'he said to cast out,' and the 'he' is Christ, as the following quotation shows.
rejected: and he said he casts out demons in the Holy Spirit

choices.english: the subjection that has been subjected in his flesh
choices.why: The participle ὑποτεταγμένης is passive, indicating the flesh is what has been subjected, not what accomplishes subjection.
rejected: the subjection accomplished in his flesh

choices.why: The term ἐμφύσημα means a breathing or breath, and the author is drawing a parallel between the Word as Son and the Spirit as God's breath.

pass_b_english: For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior (Isaiah 45:15). All who oppose him will be put to shame and disgraced. Those oppose him who do not confess that he and his Spirit are of the same being as the Father, and that besides him there is no God, and those who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty. For no one can know God unless he confesses with the apostle Thomas the one who was crucified and risen from the dead as Lord and God—the one who says to his apostles: “If you had known me, you would have known my Father also; from now on you do know him and have seen him” (John 14:7). Philip says to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that is enough for us” (John 14:8). Jesus says to him, “Have I been with you so long, and you have not known me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen my Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak I do not speak on my own. The Father who remains in me does his works. Believe me that I am in my Father and the Father is in me; or else believe because of the works themselves” (John 14:9-11). Now it was the work of God the Father to cast out demons, and he said by the Holy Spirit that he cast out demons: “But if I,” he says, “cast out demons by the Spirit of God” (Matthew 12:28). About this Luke says, “But if I cast out demons by the finger of God.” For when Scripture names Christ the arm of the Father, it calls the Holy Spirit the finger of God; and when it names the Son the Word of God, it calls the Holy Spirit the breath of God. And again the apostle says: “When he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he abolishes every rule and every authority and power. For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be abolished is death. For he has put all things in subjection under his feet. But when it says, ‘All things are put in subjection,’ it is clear that this excludes the one who put all things in subjection to him. When all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all” (1 Corinthians 15:24-28). He is speaking about the subjection of the world, the subjection accomplished in his flesh. For about his divine kingdom Daniel declared: “And of his kingdom there will be no end” (Daniel 7:14). Just as Luke says that the angel Gabriel said to the Virgin about the Lord: “And he will reign forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end” (Luke 1:33). But the apostle says his kingdom has an end. “For he must reign,” he says, “until he has put all his enemies under his feet” (1 Corinthians 15:25). In the same way David also says: “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet’” (Psalm 110:1).

problems.quote: and in the Holy Spirit he said to cast out demons
problems.source_quote: ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια
problems.why: Source says Christ said he casts out demons in the Spirit, not that 'he said to cast out demons'.
problems.fix: and he said, 'I cast out demons by the Holy Spirit'

edits.old: and in the Holy Spirit he said to cast out demons
edits.new: and he said that he casts out demons by the Holy Spirit

fixed: The source 'ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια' means Christ said he casts out demons in/by the Holy Spirit, not that he said to cast out demons. The English misstates the source, so I fixed it.

problems.quote: he said that he casts out demons by the Holy Spirit
problems.source_quote: ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια
problems.why: Source says 'he said in/by Holy Spirit to cast out demons,' not 'he said that he casts out.' The English makes it a statement about himself, but source is ambiguous: 'he said in Holy Spirit I cast out.'
problems.fix: and he said in the Holy Spirit, 'I cast out demons'

problems.quote: the subjection that has been subjected in his flesh
problems.why: Source says 'the subjection subjected in his flesh,' meaning the world's subjection accomplished in his incarnate flesh. English 'that has been subjected' loses the passive participle's sense of being made subject.
problems.fix: the subjection accomplished in his flesh

problems.quote: and who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty
problems.source_quote: καὶ οἱ τὸ πάθος αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν ἐπαισχυνόμενοι
problems.why: The English omits the connection: these opponents are also those ashamed of his passion and poverty. The 'and who' makes it a separate relative clause, but source has 'and those ashamed' as also opposing him.
problems.fix: and those who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty

problems.quote: and that besides him there is no God
problems.source_quote: καὶ πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν
problems.why: Source says 'besides him there is no God'; English adds 'that' clause but drops the negation 'no', implying the opposite.
problems.fix: and that besides him there is no God
problems.ruling: Source μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν = 'there is no God'; English drops 'no', inverting meaning.

edits.old: and he said that he casts out demons by the Holy Spirit
edits.new: and he said in the Holy Spirit, “I cast out demons”

edits.old: the subjection that has been subjected in his flesh
edits.new: the subjection accomplished in his flesh

edits.old: and who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty
edits.new: and those who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty

fixed: Changed 'he said that he casts out demons by the Holy Spirit' to 'he said in the Holy Spirit, “I cast out demons”' because the source has 'ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια' (he said in the Holy Spirit to cast out demons), not a statement about himself.

Changed 'the subjection that has been subjected in his flesh' to 'the subjection accomplished in his flesh' because the source 'τῆς ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποτεταγμένης' means the subjection accomplished in his flesh, not a subjection that has been subjected.

Changed 'and who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty' to 'and those who are ashamed of his suffering and his poverty' because the source 'καὶ οἱ τὸ πάθος αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν ἐπαισχυνόμενοι' has 'and those ashamed' as a parallel group opposing him, not a separate relative clause.
Left 'and that besides him there is no God' unchanged because the English already correctly renders the source 'καὶ πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν' with the negation 'no'.

problems.quote: he said in the Holy Spirit, "I cast out demons"
problems.source_quote: ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια
problems.why: The Greek says Jesus spoke "in the Holy Spirit" about casting out demons, not "he said in the Holy Spirit, 'I cast out demons.'" The English makes it sound like the Father spoke, but the subject is Jesus throughout.
problems.fix: and he said by the Holy Spirit that he cast out demons

problems.source_quote: Εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν δακτύλῳ Θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια
problems.why: The source does not identify this as Luke 11:20; the English adds a scripture citation not present in the source.

problems.quote: Those oppose him who do not confess that he and his Spirit are of the same being as the Father, and that besides him there is no God
problems.source_quote: καὶ πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν
problems.why: Source says 'that besides him there is no God' refers to the Spirit, not Christ; English attaches it to Christ.
problems.fix: and that besides the Spirit there is no God
problems.ruling: Greek 'αὐτοῦ' in 'πλὴν αὐτοῦ' refers back to nearest antecedent 'τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ' (his Spirit), not Christ.

problems.quote: “But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God” (Matthew 12:28).
problems.source_quote: Εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ, φησὶν, ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια
problems.why: Source attributes the quote to Christ saying it ('he says'); English drops the attribution 'he says'.
problems.fix: “But if I,” he says, “cast out demons by the Spirit of God”
problems.ruling: Greek 'φησὶν' ('he says') attributing the quote to Christ is omitted, losing the rhetorical structure.

problems.quote: and that besides him there is no God
problems.source_quote: καὶ πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν
problems.why: The Greek 'αὐτοῦ' refers to the Spirit, not Christ; the claim is that besides the Spirit there is no God.
problems.fix: and that besides the Spirit there is no God
problems.ruling: Same as #1: 'αὐτοῦ' refers to the Spirit, making 'besides the Spirit there is no God' the meaning.

edits.old: Those oppose him who do not confess that he and his Spirit are of the same being as the Father, and that besides him there is no God
edits.new: Those oppose him who do not confess that he and his Spirit are of the same being as the Father, and that besides the Spirit there is no God

edits.old: and he said in the Holy Spirit, “I cast out demons”: “But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God” (Matthew 12:28). About this Luke says, “But if I cast out demons by the finger of God” (Luke 11:20).
edits.new: and he said by the Holy Spirit that he cast out demons: “But if I,” he says, “cast out demons by the Spirit of God” (Matthew 12:28). About this Luke says, “But if I cast out demons by the finger of God.”

fixed: The Greek 'αὐτοῦ' in 'πλὴν αὐτοῦ μὴ εἶναι Θεὸν' refers to the Spirit, not Christ; the English wrongly attached 'besides him' to Christ. Fixed to 'besides the Spirit'.

The Greek 'ἐν Πνεύματι δὲ ἁγίῳ εἶπεν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια' means Jesus said by the Holy Spirit that he cast out demons, not that the Father spoke. Fixed to 'he said by the Holy Spirit that he cast out demons'.
The source does not identify the Luke quotation as Luke 11:20; the citation was added. Removed '(Luke 11:20)'.
The source has 'φησὶν' ('he says') attributing the Matthew quotation to Christ; the English dropped it. Restored 'he says'.

fixed.quote: besides the Spirit there is no God
fixed.fix: besides him there is no God
fixed.note: αὐτοῦ refers to Christ, echoing 'besides you there is no God' from Isa 45:14, not to the Spirit.

dismissed.quote: he abolishes every rule and every authority and power
dismissed.why: The Greek has 'when he abolishes' not 'he abolishes'; missing 'when' changes the temporal structure.
dismissed.note: The English already reads 'when he abolishes'; the checker quoted only part of the clause.
